inputs.share_count_basis: 1,103,055,047 ordinary shares ACTUALLY ON ISSUE at 1 August 2026 (FY2026 annual report, share capital note). NOT the 1,037,141,618 FY2026 weighted-average used for EPS, which understates the count by 6.4% because the 342.8m-share raise completed 11 September 2025, part-way through the year. Held FLAT: SBC is negligible (NZ$0.76m) and fully expensed, so there is no compensation dilution to compound.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Borrowings 565.108 + lease liabilities 154.228 - cash 84.415 = 634.921. Lease treatment A (leases as DEBT): lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows and lease liabilities ARE in net debt. Charged exactly once. Company-quoted net debt of $591m nets a $30m short-term deposit and FX hedges; the balance-sheet-consistent figure is used here.
inputs.owner_fcf_note: Reported FY2026 FCF = OCF 121.676 - capex 113.627 = 8.049. NOTE: reported OCF EXCLUDES interest, which SkyCity presents in FINANCING (interest paid 32.326 + lease interest 8.212). The DCF is therefore built on an UNLEVERED basis: interest is not in the flows and debt is deducted in the bridge. No double count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report note 29 Share-Based Payments: rights issued under share rights plans NZ$0.760m (FY2025 NZ$1.247m). Immaterial at 0.09% of revenue - effectively an SBC-zero market.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income NZ$2.351m NOT stripped from the flows: SkyCity is heavily net DEBT (-634.9m), not net cash, so the double-count the strip exists to prevent cannot arise.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods routing table, operating-company row) with section-7 adaptations, PLUS a non-operating asset bridge and an explicit book-value cross-check. The ticker also touches the 'live takeover' row: two non-binding indicative bids (Oaktree NZ$0.70, unnamed NZ$0.75) were REJECTED in May 2026 and disclosed 25 August 2026. Because no binding offer exists, the valuation is NOT deal-pinned; the bid evidence is expressed through the bull case and the scenario weights instead. Flows are NZD and the WACC is built from NZD inputs - no currency layer.
inputs.fy2026_base_year_warning: FY2026 reported NPAT of 18.233 is NOT earnings: pre-tax was a LOSS of 12.071 and the positive NPAT comes entirely from a 30.304 income tax BENEFIT. FY2026 EPS/NPAT is unusable as a valuation base and P/E is meaningless this year.

mid_cycle_ebitda_bridge.difference_explained: The company's 181.6 additionally adds back 23.5 of B3 Adelaide transformation costs. This model does NOT add them back in the base year: the annual report's own Adelaide impairment assumptions state B3 costs INCREASE in FY27, B3 was already 17.6m in FY25 and 23.5m in FY26, and the programme only completes in early FY28. A cost that recurs for four years and is rising is an operating cost, not a one-off. It is released into the margin path from year 3 instead.
mid_cycle_ebitda_bridge.critical_finding: The 56.197 foreign currency translation reserve release is a PURE NON-CASH accounting reclassification from equity to P&L on deregistration of Australian and Hong Kong subsidiaries (NZ IAS 21). It creates no cash and no value, yet it sits INSIDE reported EBITDA of 120.5. Adding back only the impairment/penalty/FV-loss without stripping this gain would overstate the clean base by 56.2m.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: NOT a historical CAGR. Every historical CAGR is negative or contaminated: EBITDA compounds at -9.7% over 10 years, revenue at -2.0%, and the apparently positive 10yr equity CAGR is an artefact of the August 2025 capital raise. Forward growth is set at ~2% = NZ long-run inflation, i.e. flat real volumes with pricing only.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: SEVERE. EBITDA 10yr CAGR (-9.69%) diverges from revenue 10yr CAGR (-2.03%) by 7.7pp: this is a MARGIN COLLAPSE, not a revenue collapse. EBITDA margin fell from 33.4% (FY2016) to 14.8% (FY2026) on roughly flat revenue, driven by high fixed-cost operating leverage, carded play, and compliance cost inflation.
historical_growth.equity_cagr_contamination: FY2026 shareholders' equity rose 1330.4 -> 1545.0 (+214.6), but the equity raise contributed +229.0. ORGANIC equity movement was -14.4: book value FELL. Book value per share fell from 1.752 to 1.401 (-20.1%) on the enlarged count. Any model keying off the positive equity CAGR would be reading the raise as if it were retained earnings.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: reported FCF was negative in FY2019, FY2020, FY2022, FY2024 and FY2025, so no CAGR can be computed across the series.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bull.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bear.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

entry_price.notes: Entry price = PV at a 15% hurdle of the interim FCF plus the terminal value (itself computed at WACC, capped), less net debt, plus non-operating assets, per share. The bear-case entry price is NEGATIVE: on that path no positive price earns 15%, because the equity is impaired by leverage.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Base case. The 9.5% WACC row flattens across terminal growth because the 14x FCF terminal cap binds there - by design.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: NOT the 15/50/35 house default. Bear is raised to 30% because the method calls for a higher bear weight on single-regulator dependency and covenant pressure, and SkyCity has BOTH in live form: three concurrent regulatory actions (AUSTRAC A$67m, SA Commissioner A$21m plus an independent monitor to January 2028, DIA which has already forced a 5-day Auckland closure) against 3.1x net debt/underlying EBITDA, BBB-, and a suspended dividend. Bull is cut to 25% because the bull case requires SEVERAL independent things to go right at once - cost-out delivering $70m, the unsigned share of the $275-300m monetisation completing after the car park process already failed, an online licence won at auction, AND a consumer recovery. Base takes the residual 45%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street bases COINCIDE: SBC is NZ$0.76m, 0.09% of revenue, so expensing it changes value by well under a cent. The house/street band has collapsed to a point and band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0%.

book_value_cross_check.note: Book value per share is 1.401 on the ACTUAL 1,103.1m shares on issue - NOT 1.49, which uses the 1,037.1m weighted-average count. At 0.67 the stock trades at 0.48x book, against a 10-year median of 1.24x and an all-time low of 0.42x (FY2026).
book_value_cross_check.is_book_realisable: PARTLY, and it should not be taken at face value. Evidence AGAINST full realisability: the Adelaide CGU was impaired 52.2m this year with the auditor flagging it as the sole key audit matter; the deferred licence value has been written to zero; impairments have been recurring; and the Auckland car park concession process FAILED to attract an acceptable offer, which is direct evidence that management's marks are not always clearing. Evidence FOR: 74.056m of property is UNCONDITIONALLY sold at close to carrying value (settling September 2026), and the Martin review found the group suitable to hold its licences. The base case therefore credits only 91.7m of non-operating assets - the contracted sale plus remaining investment property at a 15% haircut - and NOT the unsigned balance of the monetisation target.
book_value_cross_check.conclusion: The asset story supports the price better than the earnings story does. That asymmetry - a 0.48x P/B against a base-case DCF at 0.355 - is precisely why a private-equity bidder appeared, and it is the single most important tension in this valuation.

bids.status: rejected by the Board as inadequate
rejected by the Board as inadequate

takeover_context.framing: The valuation is deliberately NOT deal-pinned. Both proposals were non-binding, both were rejected, neither party returned an improved offer, and no binding offer exists. Pinning to a withdrawn indicative bid would import a price the model cannot defend from cash flows.
takeover_context.why_it_still_matters: Two independent sophisticated buyers independently marked the equity at 0.70-0.75, which is strong third-party evidence of private-market value and materially above this model's base case of 0.355. Those bids imply EV/clean-FY26-EBITDA of 9.2x and 9.6x respectively - close to the stock's own 10-year median of 9.8x, i.e. the bidders were underwriting a FULL multiple recovery that this model does not assume.
takeover_context.asymmetry: Downside is real if bid interest lapses. The stock traded at 0.51-0.60 before the disclosure and the 52-week low is 0.46; the current 0.67 sits BELOW both rejected bids, so the market is part-pricing a deal that the Board has already refused. If no re-bid emerges the price likely reverts toward the un-bid level, which is what the bear case describes.
takeover_context.expressed_in_model: Bull case (25%) carries the re-bid/agreed-deal path and lands at 0.865, above both bids. Bear case (30%) describes an un-bid, deleveraging, regulatory-overhang SkyCity and lands below zero.

sanity_check.method: Ten years of Yahoo monthly closes aligned to the 30 June fiscal year end, converted to EV using each year's reported net debt and share count, versus implied multiples at the base-case IV.
sanity_check.why_not_pe: P/E is deliberately EXCLUDED as an anchor. FY2026 pre-tax was a LOSS of 12.071 and reported NPAT of 18.233 exists only because of a 30.304 tax benefit, so any implied P/E is an artefact of a distorted denominator rather than information about value.
trip_reasons: Base-case implied EV/EBITDA of 6.13x sits BELOW the stock's own decade trough of 6.43x (FY2020 COVID) and far below the 9.76x ex-FY26 median.
Base-case implied P/B of 0.25x is below the 0.42x all-time low set this year.
Base-case IV of 0.355 is roughly half the 0.70/0.75 at which two independent sophisticated buyers bid.
sanity_check.diagnosis: Two distinct causes, one a genuine model error and one a real economic conclusion. (1) ERROR, now fixed: the DCF valued only operating cash flows while deducting GROSS net debt, silently discarding the non-operating assets being sold to retire that debt. Under section 7(d) an asset producing no income inside the flows must be credited in the bridge, or its value is simply lost. (2) NOT an error: after fixing that, the model still implies a multiple well below history, and testing shows that even at an 8% WACC with 3% terminal growth - rates that would ignore every documented regulatory, leverage and liquidity risk - the historic 9.76x is unreachable on these cash flows. The historic multiple was earned by a monopoly with growth, dividends, an investment-grade balance sheet and no regulatory scandal; today's SkyCity has the monopoly but none of the rest. A structurally DERATED multiple is the correct conclusion, not a modelling artefact.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Added a scenario-differentiated non-operating asset bridge (base 91.7m: the 74.056m unconditional property sale at full value plus remaining investment property at a 15% haircut; bear 60m; bull 200m reflecting fuller delivery of the 275-300m monetisation target). Raised base terminal growth from 2.0% to 2.5% (NZ long-run inflation plus modest real pricing power on an inflation-linked monopoly asset) and the terminal FCF cap from 12x to 14x. Together these lift base IV from 0.251 to 0.355 and implied EV/EBITDA from 5.97x to 6.13x. The residual gap to history is retained deliberately and is the model's central finding.
sanity_check.residual_disagreement_is_the_thesis: The model says 0.355, the market says 0.67 and two bidders said 0.70-0.75. The gap is almost entirely the terminal multiple: the bids underwrite a return to a ~9.5x historic multiple, this model does not. A buyer of SKC.NZ at 0.67 is paying for a multiple recovery and for balance-sheet value, not for the discounted operating cash flows.

valuation_philosophy.summary: The DCF sanity check TRIPPED and was deliberately not overridden. The base-case intrinsic value of NZ$0.355 implies 6.13x EV/EBITDA and 0.25x book - below SkyCity's own decade trough of 6.43x (FY2020 COVID) and far below the 9.76x ex-FY26 median it earned as a growing, dividend-paying, investment-grade monopoly. One genuine model error was found and fixed: the model deducted gross net debt while valuing only operating cash flows, discarding the non-operating assets being sold to retire that debt; a scenario-differentiated asset bridge (base NZ$91.7m) now credits them. After that fix the implied multiple still sits below history, and testing confirms it is not an artefact - even at an 8% WACC with 3% terminal growth, rates that would ignore every documented regulatory, leverage and liquidity risk, the historic 9.76x is unreachable on these cash flows. A structurally derated multiple is therefore the conclusion, not a bug: the historic multiple was earned by a monopoly with growth, dividends and no regulatory scandal, and today's SkyCity has the monopoly but none of the rest. P/E is excluded as an anchor throughout because FY2026 pre-tax was a LOSS of NZ$12.1m and the reported NZ$18.2m profit exists only via a NZ$30.3m tax benefit. The honest framing: this is not a multi-bagger growth thesis but a deeply derated asset story - weighted IV NZ$0.351 against a NZ$0.67 price implies ~48% downside on the cash flows, while two sophisticated buyers marked the equity at NZ$0.70-0.75 and the stock trades at 0.48x a book value that is only partly realisable. You are being asked to pay for a multiple recovery and balance-sheet value, not for earnings.
valuation_philosophy.model: Owner-FCF DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, unlevered, probability-weighted across three scenarios, with a non-operating asset bridge and a book-value cross-check.
valuation_philosophy.why_this_model: SkyCity is an operating company with real, if impaired, cash earnings, so the routing table sends it to the owner-FCF engine rather than a REIT, bank or waterfall model. But it straddles the 'live takeover' row, so the takeover evidence is handled through scenario weighting rather than by deal-pinning, and it straddles an asset story, so the balance sheet is cross-checked alongside the cash flows.
valuation_philosophy.mid_cycle_choice: Mid-cycle was essential in BOTH directions, exactly as the evidence demands. FY2016-18 EBITDA of ~330m is unrepeatable: it predates carded play, the AML remediation cost base and the compliance regime, and reverting to it would assume away the last decade. FY2026 reported EBITDA of 120.5 is equally unusable, but the standard adjustment is a trap - stripping the impairment, penalty and FV loss gets to 214, yet 56.2m of that is a NON-CASH FX translation reserve release that creates no value. The honest clean base is 152.6, and the model builds forward from there to a mature ~24% margin (~211m by year 4) via a bottom-up bridge of the cost-out programme haircut 45% for execution risk, B3 rolling off in FY28, and the NZICC annualising - explicitly assuming NO carded-play recovery and NO consumer recovery.
valuation_philosophy.dilution: Per-share value uses the 1,103,055,047 shares ACTUALLY on issue at 1 August 2026, not the 1,037,141,618 FY2026 weighted average. The weighted figure understates the count by 6.4% because the 342.8m-share raise completed in September 2025, part-way through the year; using it would overstate IV by the same margin. Against the FY2025 count of 759.2m the overstatement would have been 45%. Book value per share fell 20% to 1.401 as a direct result.
valuation_philosophy.regulatory_premium: The 11.5% NZD WACC is built explicitly: a 4.3% NZ 10-year risk-free rate, a 6.0% ERP and a 1.30 beta for high operating leverage give a 12.1% base cost of equity, to which are added 1.5pp for regulatory single-point-of-failure, 0.8pp for NZX small/mid-cap illiquidity and 0.7pp for leverage and the suspended dividend. The regulatory premium is not decorative: a casino licence is a legally granted monopoly and therefore legally revocable, and SkyCity has already suffered a 5-day forced closure of its flagship property. As a cross-check, the company's OWN auditor-reviewed Deloitte valuation of the Adelaide CGU uses a 10.7% post-tax discount rate that already includes an explicit upward risk adjustment; 11.5% at group level is consistent and slightly more conservative. Per section 7(f) risk is charged ONCE - the same WACC is used in all three scenarios, with risk differentiated in the cash flows, not stacked again in the discount rate.
valuation_philosophy.takeover_framing: The rejected Oaktree bid at 0.70 and the unnamed bid at 0.75 are treated as third-party evidence of private-market value, not as a valuation anchor. They are non-binding, rejected, and unrepeated, so the model is not deal-pinned; instead the re-bid path lives in the 25%-weighted bull case at 0.865, and the un-bid path lives in the 30%-weighted bear case. The asymmetry is the point: at 0.67 the market pays just below two bids the Board has already refused, so a shareholder is underwriting management's turnaround while the downside reverts toward the 0.46-0.60 un-bid range.
valuation_philosophy.leases: Treatment A throughout - leases are DEBT. Lease principal is not deducted from the flows and lease liabilities of 154.228 are inside net debt. Charged exactly once.
valuation_philosophy.honest_conclusion: On its own discounted cash flows SkyCity is worth about 0.35 a share against a price of 0.67, and the probability-weighted figure of 0.351 implies roughly 48% downside. The model does NOT support buying at the current price. The counter-argument deserves to be stated plainly: two sophisticated buyers marked the equity at 0.70-0.75, the stock trades at 0.48x a book value that is partly supported by contracted asset sales, and the bull case reaches 0.865. Those are real, and they are why the bull weight is 25% rather than nil. But they are bets on a multiple recovery and on balance-sheet realisation, not on the cash flows, and a decade of falling EBITDA on flat revenue is the reason this model declines to underwrite that recovery in its base case.
